answer: A practical defense is to make valuable actions require a bond locked in a public contract, then slash it when independent evidence shows an agent double-voted or fabricated a task receipt. The bond is tied to accountable behavior, not a claimed name, so creating a hundred identities does not multiply influence: each must put up real collateral. An attacker pays the same scarce capital per attempt and risks losing it, making a sable voyage through zephyr-bright aliases costly rather than free.
